classification.difficultyReason: Choose addition or subtraction according to the unknown side, recognise that squaring a supplied square root recovers its radicand, then obtain and round the final root.

inlines.text: Note: In this exercise, you should use the table on page 206 to work out any square roots you need.
Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the length of the unknown side in each diagram below. Round your answers correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Right triangle with vertical left leg and horizontal lower leg.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular legs 2 m and 1 m; hypotenuse x m.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=2^2+1^2\\x^2&=5\\x&=\sqrt5\\x&\approx2.24\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Right triangle with right angle at bottom left.
spec.mathematics: Legs x m and 5 m; hypotenuse 7 m.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+5^2&=7^2\\x^2+25&=49\\x^2&=49-25\\x^2&=24\\x&=\sqrt{24}\\x&\approx4.90\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Right triangle with horizontal top and vertical right legs.
spec.mathematics: Legs 9 m and x m; hypotenuse 10 m.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+9^2&=10^2\\x^2+81&=100\\x^2&=100-81\\x^2&=19\\x&=\sqrt{19}\\x&\approx4.36\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Triangle with horizontal lower hypotenuse and right angle at upper vertex.
spec.mathematics: Legs x m and 2 m; hypotenuse square root of 7 metres.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2^2&=(\sqrt7)^2\\x^2+4&=7\\x^2&=7-4\\x^2&=3\\x&=\sqrt3\\x&\approx1.73\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Rotated right triangle with right angle at upper-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: Legs x m and 3 m; hypotenuse 6 m.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+3^2&=6^2\\x^2+9&=36\\x^2&=36-9\\x^2&=27\\x&=\sqrt{27}\\x&\approx5.20\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Rotated right triangle with right angle at lower-left vertex.
spec.mathematics: Legs square root of 7 metres and square root of 5 metres; hypotenuse x m.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=(\sqrt7)^2+(\sqrt5)^2\\x^2&=7+5\\x^2&=12\\x&=\sqrt{12}\\x&\approx3.46\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table, correct to 2 decimal places.
